newsitem.title: INDIA: India HPCL in 115.0 bln rupee projects.
newsitem.headline: India HPCL in 115.0 bln rupee projects.

text.p: India's state-run refiner Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) said it planned to spend 115.0 billion rupees until 2000/01 in new projects.
"Our entire funding is in place upto 2000/1," said C. Ramulu, HPCL's executive director.
New projects on hand include new refineries on the west coast and the northern Punjab state and expansion of its existing refining capacities.
HPCL chairman H.L. Zutshi said Oman Oil Company had opted to pull out of the proposed west coast refinery because of its other commitments.
"We have several enquiries from global oil majors which are now under consideration (as partner in this refinery)," he said.
HPCL and Oman Oil were to own 26 percent each in the west coast refinery company.
Saudi's Aramco will partner HPCL in the Punjab refinery project. Both refineries would each have capacities to process six million tonnes of crude oil per year.
HPCL's current refining capacity is 13.0 million tonnes of crude a year, which is expected to rise to 34 million tonnes after the new projects are commissioned.
